6 Cyl Envoy Block ,Head Bolts break on removal.
At least the broken parts aren't recessed, and the engine is out of the vehicle already. You have to look on the bright side with these things.
I posted mainly for an FYI if anyone takes a head off expect this to happen, doesn't happen on any other ones that i am aware of.

so this happens everytime?

maybe the bolts are being over torqued from factory?

They are torque to yield bolts and cant be reused so they are stretched to the max. I have done thousands on other engines but this one is unique for this problem. So if anyone is quoting a job consider some extra work on this engine. It seems the bolt is being stretched and jamming the top couple threads in the block causing the breakage. They come out fine after by drilling a hole in them but it does add to the work time and not a great way to un-torque a cyl head.

Oh, those are just joyous engines to remove heads on; so are the 5 cylinder engines used in the Colorado/canyon trucks. The head bolts are about a 3/8 diameter that is close to 7 inches long, and they are designed to stretch during torqueing; this makes them act like a spring to maintain a constant clamp load on the head gasket, but it also weakens the shank so they break off if you try to disassemble them. GM has a TSB which says to shock them by striking the head with a hammer several times before attempting removal, but some of them always still snap off anyway during removal.. Just to make it more fun, if you need to use a tap to clean up the threads of the block after drilling and extracting the bolts, you will find the thread is a weird pitch (like a 10 x 2.00 or something equally strange) and the tap is only available through Kent-Moore. If you find yourself in a bind and are friends with someone at your local GM dealer, the tap is part of the line engine SST tool set that all dealerships are required to have.
